regime: Rotation / Split Tape (NQ flips short, commodities lead)
summary: Rotation day with a split tape and nothing on the US calendar. The story was under the surface. NQ ground up to a 29,985 overnight high, then sold off through the entire US session and closed 29,763.75 (-0.26%), losing its trend stop on the close and flipping short. The S&P held up better, essentially flat at 7,777 and still above its stop, so the two indices split instead of moving together. The real action was in commodities. Gold extended its uptrend to 4,416.5 (+1.10%) and crude exploded +6.75% to 82.29, the day's big mover, clearing its stop with room to spare on Middle East supply headlines. The VIX firmed to 15.46 (+3.76%) and the 10-year yield ticked up to about 4.71%, a mild risk-off lean under a calm-looking surface. Money rotated out of the Nasdaq and into hard assets with July CPI two days out.
psychology: Today was a lesson in the overnight trap and respecting a trend change. NQ spent the whole overnight session grinding higher to 29,985, close enough to 30,000 to get people excited. Then the US session opened and it went one way: down, most of the day, into a short flip on the close. If you bought the overnight high because it looked strong, you spent the session underwater. Overnight strength in a thin August session is the lowest-conviction kind of strength, because it is built on light volume and can unwind the moment real size shows up at the US open. The discipline is simple: let the regular session confirm an overnight move before you trust it. And when your trend stop actually flips, like NQ's did today, that is information. You do not have to flip your bias with it, but you do have to stop treating the long side as the easy side. The traders who got hurt today decided overnight that NQ was going to 30,000 and refused to update when the tape said otherwise.

event.name: No scheduled release: money rotates from tech into hard assets
event.consensus: No top-tier US release was scheduled for Monday, August 10. The week's driver is July CPI on Wednesday, August 12 at 8:30 AM ET.
event.actual: With nothing on the calendar, the day was about positioning ahead of CPI, and the positioning was a rotation. The Nasdaq gave back its overnight gains and flipped its trend short, while the S&P held up and closed flat. That split, tech soft and the broad index steady, is the tell that this was rotation rather than broad selling.
event.surprise: The VIX firming to 15.46 (+3.76%) and the 10-year yield ticking up to about 4.71% both fit a market taking a little risk off the table before the inflation print.
event.nqReaction: NQ built its highs overnight at 29,985, broke up out of its opening range to 29,874.5, then reversed and sold off all session to close 29,763.75, back inside and below its range and below its trend stop, flipping short.
event.crossAsset: Gold extended its uptrend to 4,416.5 (+1.10%) and crude was the day's outlier, up +6.75% to 82.29. Reporting tied crude's jump to Middle East supply headlines: Iran escalating its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a claimed Houthi attack on a Saudi refinery, and a weekend tanker attack in the Hormuz area, a geopolitical risk premium that outweighed a recent OPEC+ quota increase. Crude cleared its stop decisively and is now stretched.

risk.sizing: Realized volatility is still low, with NQ's ATR down to 81.84, so risk per contract is smaller than last week. But the board is no longer aligned. NQ flipped short below 29,958, ES is long by only 13 points above 7,764, and the two commodities are strong but stretched longs. A split tape is harder to trade than a one-way day, so size down and let conditions come to you.
risk.openRisk: Treat ES as the swing vote: if it loses 7,764 it likely joins NQ lower; if it holds and reclaims 7,779 the split can persist. Crude is a strong trend but very extended after a +6.75% headline-driven day, so chasing it here is the low-quality trade; a pullback toward its 81.56 average is the cleaner with-trend spot.

All four opening ranges broke UP first, then split. NQ's up-break failed (broke to 29,874.5, closed 29,763.75 back inside and below its range). ES broke up to 7,787 and closed flat inside its range. Gold and crude held their breaks and ran. NQ's opening range was wide at 122.25 points, about 1.49x its 81.84 ATR, so the first move up was lower quality, which is how it resolved.
